# Inner Products

::: {#exr-p1-inner-prod} 
> Consider the vector space $P_1$ over $\mathbb R$.
> Does the function $I : P_1 \to \mathbb R$ given by 
> 
> $$
> I(p ,q ) := \int_{0}^{1} p(x) q(x) x \, dx 
> $$
> 
> define an inner product on $P_1$?
> Make sure to verify all of the inner product properties or show that one is not satisfied.
:::

::: {#exr-inner-prod-from-just-len} 
> Find an inner product on $\mathbb R^2$ such that $(1,0)$ has length 2 and $(1,1)$ has length 3.

> Do a computation to demonstrate that your inner product has these two properties.
:::

::: {#exr-plane-projection} 
> Given
> $$
> x := \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}
> $$
> 
> in $\mathbb R^3$ with the dot product, compute the part of $x$ orthogonal to the plane spanned by
> 
> $$
> \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \text{and}
> \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.
> $$
:::

<!-- gram schmit -->
::: {#exr-matrix-solve-1} 
> Consider the vector space $P_2$ over $\mathbb R$.
> Consider the inner product $I : P_2 \to \mathbb R$ given by 
> 
> $$
> I(p ,q ) := \int_{0}^{1} p(x) q(x) \, dx 
> $$
> 
> (you do not need to show that this is an inner product).
> 
> Find an orthonormal basis for $P_2$ with regard to this inner product.
:::
